spans.s:
pīṭha
(‘seat’)
------------------------------------------
In a general sense it means a thing upon which one sits.
However, in a technical sense, it indicates the pedestal of an icon.
The shape and the size of a पीठ depend upon the style of the temple—such as नागर, वेसर or drāviḍa—as also the posture of the image. It is square for a seated (āsīna) image. It can be rectangular or circular or even oval, if the image is in the स्थानक (standing) pose.
The height may be 12 aṅgulas (See AṄGULA.) or just ⅕ the height of the image. In the case of Śivaliṅgas, it should be 4 or 5 times the diameter of the cylindrical shaft.
Iconographical works describe pīṭhas of several designs such as भद्रपीठ or पद्मपीठ which give enough scope to the sculptor to exhibit his skills.
The word पीठ is sometimes used to indicate a Śaktipīṭha, a place of पिल्ग्रिमगे connected with शक्ति or मोथेर्-goddess. (See TANTRAS for details.)
If it is used as a suffix, it gives different meanings. For example: बलिपीठ (sacrificial altar); Śāradāpīṭha (the monastic centre of Advaita Vedānta at Śṛṅgerī, Karnataka) and so on.
